governing_thought: Information science is divided by the stage in the life of a record, from creation to keeping: creation and publication, description, arrangement, retrieval and use, and preservation and governance.
dimension: the stage in the life of a record
rank_note: The stages run in the order a record passes through them, from its creation to its long-term keeping.

pillars.title: Creation and publication
pillars.statement: Creation and publication is the stage in which records come into being, are produced and are issued to their audiences.

pillars.title: Description
pillars.statement: Description is the stage in which a record is named, listed and indexed so that its content and subject are represented.

pillars.title: Arrangement
pillars.statement: Arrangement is the stage in which described records are ordered into classes by classification systems, theory and control structures.

pillars.title: Retrieval and use
pillars.statement: Retrieval and use is the stage in which arranged records are stored, searched for, found and used by their readers.

pillars.title: Preservation and governance
pillars.statement: Preservation and governance is the final stage in which records are kept, protected and managed over the long term.

method_line.title: Method line
method_line.covers: how the discipline is studied, taught and recorded
